# ModDotPlot Browser v0.9.1

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

v0.9.1 makes the bundled *Arabidopsis thaliana* example fast without substituting a
different scientific result. Its default Chr1 self plot is delivered as a 255,582-byte
precomputed refined overview. The full raw FASTA remains available on the same origin
through strict indexed byte-range reads for interactions outside that cache, and the
CEN180 annotation is removed from the startup fetch set.

See the [validation record](v0.9.1/VALIDATION.md) for the completed integrated release
checks on this isolated source copy.

## Precomputed default Chr1 overview

The checked-in `Col-CEN_v1.2.Chr1.mdp-overview-v1.gz` artifact contains the complete
default Chr1-versus-Chr1 overview:

* 1,000 by 1,000 cells in 16 clipped 256-cell tiles;
* refined 1,024-register estimates with `k=21`;
* identity, orientation direction, and direction-support channels; and
* all seven sequence records from the exact bundled FAI.

The uncompressed versioned payload is 6,003,800 bytes and deterministic gzip reduces
it to 255,582 bytes (about 250 KiB). It is generated by
`scripts/generate-arabidopsis-overview.mjs`; `--check` regenerates it and requires a
byte-for-byte match with the checked-in artifact.

Palette, background, and guide changes reuse these numeric tiles immediately. Sequence
bases are not required until an interaction asks for data outside the default overview
or the runtime caches.

## Exact artifact and scientific compatibility

Before decoding, startup verifies the artifact against a pinned SHA-256 and requires
the separately retrieved 195-byte FAI to match its embedded index exactly. It accepts
the exact 255,582-byte gzip representation or the exact 6,003,800-byte payload exposed
when a static server applies transparent HTTP gzip decoding; each representation has
its own pinned size and SHA-256.
The artifact carries a versioned magic value, literal FAI text, complete source-asset
manifest, comparison identity, tile descriptors, and both the readable scientific
fields and the full canonical scientific-configuration identity. The decoder verifies
the gzip stream, all lengths and shapes, SHA-256 field formats, FAI/sequence agreement,
configuration digest/identity agreement, tile provenance, non-overlap, and complete
matrix coverage.

Before publishing a tile, the worker constructs the requested configuration with the
current Wasm engine and requires its full canonical identity and digest to match the
artifact exactly. A matching short digest alone is insufficient. An incompatible or
malformed artifact cannot be presented as a current computed result.

The checked-in compressed artifact has SHA-256:

```text
cff868954355763b81df5e3ac097120f24d4664213a9005677c27bf9b8dd0d4b
```

The canonical decoded envelope has SHA-256:

```text
82701ff40df42b075c50dd3d2b60f28be11a35cafe89647d0b3e6201748ebdd0
```

Its scientific configuration digest is `bc5c5131ad1c9a20`.

## Raw FASTA only for uncached interactions

The bundled raw `Col-CEN_v1.2.fasta` is no longer downloaded in full before the default
plot. A request that cannot be satisfied by precomputed or runtime-cached data—such as
another chromosome, a pairwise/grid comparison, uncached zoom detail, exact mode, or a
sequence-derived track—uses the embedded FAI to request only the necessary raw FASTA
byte range. Once validated and packed, that sequence remains resident for reuse during
the browser session.

The range source accepts only same-origin URLs and strict `206 Partial Content`
responses. It verifies `Content-Range` coordinates and total length, rejects content
encoding and cross-origin redirects, preserves ETag or Last-Modified with `If-Range`,
and propagates cancellation. If a server ignores `Range` and returns `200 OK`, the
browser cancels that body rather than silently downloading the entire genome.

Static deployments must therefore serve the bundled FASTA from the application origin
with HTTP byte-range support. These are ordinary requests to that static host; no
application API or external genome service is introduced.

Avoiding the full startup transfer also means the browser cannot recompute the pinned
whole-FASTA SHA-256 before first paint. The release therefore treats its same-origin
FASTA, FAI, and overview as one atomic static asset set. Strong ETag or Last-Modified
validators prevent ranges from different revisions being mixed during a session;
deployers must publish the three files together rather than replacing one in place.

## Deferred CEN180 annotation

`ColCEN_CEN180.gff3` no longer delays startup of the default overview. Its same-origin
retrieval and browser-local parsing start separately after the workspace opens and do
not gate plot publication. When ready, it appears
as the existing single logical `ColCEN_CEN180` row and automatically follows every
matching chromosome. Annotation geometry and matching rules are unchanged from v0.9.0.

## Compatibility and rollback

User-selected local FASTA/index loading, scientific estimation, exact rendering,
pairwise/grid behavior, annotation semantics, exports, palettes, and cursor guides are
unchanged from v0.9.0. The complete `moddotplot-interactive-0.9.0-source` tree remains
available on port 4180 while this release runs on port 4181.
